titration-curve.def: A graph of pH against volume of titrant added. Its steep rise (or fall) is centered on the equivalence point; its shape shows whether the acid or base is strong or weak.

half-equivalence.def: The point in a weak acid (or weak base) titration where half the analyte has reacted, at half the equivalence volume. There [HA] = [A⁻], so pH = pKa.

buffer-region.def: The flat, slowly rising part of a weak acid or weak base titration curve before the equivalence point, where the weak species and its conjugate are both present.

polyprotic.def: An acid that can give up more than one proton, one at a time (diprotic H₂A, triprotic H₃A). Each proton has its own Ka, and a titration curve can show one equivalence point per proton.
